chunks: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was asked: “Which wealth is best?” He said: “A crop which its owner has sown, cultivated, and paid its due on the day of its harvest.”
It was said: “O Messenger of Allah, then which wealth is best after crops?” He said: “A man among his sheep, having followed with them the places of rainfall, establishing salat and giving zakat.”
It was said: “O Messenger of Allah, then which wealth is best after sheep?” He said: “Cattle; they go forth with خير and return with خير.”

It was said: “O Messenger of Allah, then which wealth is best after cattle?” He said: “Those firmly rooted in the mud, those that provide food in drought. Excellent indeed is the date-palm. Whoever sells it, then its price is only like ashes upon the top of a lofty height.”
“The wind intensified against it on a stormy day.”
“Except that he replaces it in its place.”

It was said: “O Messenger of Allah, then which wealth is best after date-palms?” So he remained silent. Then a man said to him: “Then where are camels?” He said: “In them are hardship, roughness, toil, and remoteness of abode. They go forth turning away and return turning away. Their benefit does not come except from their left side. Indeed, they are never without the wretched, the wicked.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat performed and maintained by the shepherd
key_terms.الْإِبِلُ: camels, described here in connection with hardship
key_terms.حَقَّهُ: its due right, referring to the obligatory due at harvest
key_terms.زَرْعٌ: cultivated crop sown and tended by its owner

ai.seo_question: Which kinds of wealth did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله consider best?
ai.summary: This hadith ranks forms of wealth, beginning with cultivated crops, then sheep tended with devotion to salat and zakat, then cattle, and then date-palms. It also portrays date-palms as especially blessed and enduring wealth, while describing camels as associated with hardship and roughness.
